1 / 14Overall Goal

We started with your five questions

Your words

The redesign should make it much easier for a new visitor to quickly answer:

  • What does TPTC offer?
  • Which program is right for me/my child?
  • How do I register?
  • How do I become a member?
  • How do I book a court?

The goal is to move from an information-heavy website to a clear, user-friendly customer journey.

What we built

Each question has a page of its own, and each page answers it on its first screen. Here are the five, with the answer and the next step marked. Try each one.

12 / 14Reduce Information Overload

Seven things you wanted to move away from

  1. Long paragraphs → Short sections

    The longest paragraph on the whole site is 57 words, on Leagues & Events: who may join.

  2. Repeated information → One central resource

    The FAQ. Each of its 33 answers is written once and linked from the pages that need it.

  3. Multiple registration instructions → One registration process

    Register Now. A few quick questions show the exact steps on JustBookIt, then one button takes you there. The steps are written out on that page and nowhere else.

  4. Huge program pages → Individual program pages

    Your current Programs and Lessons page covers juniors and adults together, and your Camps page covers every camp. Here each program and each camp season has a page of its own, nine in all.

  5. Text-heavy pages → Cards, images and clear headings

    Every page is built from the same few parts. A heading that asks one question, cards, a table where numbers need comparing, and a frame for one photograph.

  6. Old seasonal information → Current information only

    Past dates are labelled with their year, as in Summer 2026, and kept only for reference. Dates not yet announced say Club to confirm instead of showing last year’s.

  7. Coach biographies buried in programs → Dedicated Coaches page

    Our Coaches has them all. Program pages carry one line and a link.

One registration process

Your words

Multiple registration instructions → One registration process

What we built

Register Now asks who is playing and what for, one question at a time, then shows the exact steps for that program on JustBookIt and one button, Continue on JustBookIt. Programs, camps and memberships all start in the same place. Pro National, private lessons and leagues are each shown their own first step.

14 / 14Design Direction

The one thing we left for you to decide

Your words

It should feel like a modern, professional tennis club, rather than a traditional recreation-centre website.

The new website should feel: Professional, Modern, Energetic, Family-friendly, Competitive when appropriate, Community-oriented

What we built

We let the game do the decorating. The red line on every page is the net. When a parent picks an age on the junior page, the court drawn beside it grows with the child. Dates sit on one line that runs from the outdoor season into the Dome. Competitive stays where it belongs, so High Performance is the only page set in navy.

Your list of eight things to use follows, with what the site does about each. How the whole thing should look is the one part we left open, and that is the choice waiting at the end of this page.

  1. Large, high-quality tennis photography

    Every page keeps a large frame for one photograph. The ones in the demo are stand-ins and each is labelled Placeholder image. We have written a brief for all 31 photographs, so one session at the club can replace them.

  2. Strong typography

    One serif for headings and one plain face for everything else, the same on every page.

  3. Plenty of white space

    White is the ground of the site. Navy is kept for High Performance and the foot of each page.

  4. Shorter sections

    One heading and one idea to a section. No paragraph on the site is longer than 57 words.

  5. Clear buttons

    Red is kept for the buttons that register. Every other button names where it leads.

  6. Program cards

    The four doors on Home, the level cards on Junior Recreational, the three steps on High Performance.

  7. Consistent page layouts

    Every page opens the same way. Where you are, what the page is for, then its main button.

  8. Simple registration pathways

    Register now is on every page, and every Register button leads to the same short set of choices.

The one thing we need from you

Which of these feels like your club?

These are three ways of dressing the same site. Everything you have just read stays as it is, the pages, the menu, the words. The typefaces, the colour, the photography and the way things move are what differ. For each we show the Home page, the High Performance page and the phone.

AClubhouse

The club’s 75 years lead the way. A classic serif, the founding year on every page, and four drawn courts that serve by the rules of tennis.

Leans on your wordsA Community Since 1951. Community-oriented. Family-friendly.

BDome

The club under the Dome. Deep night green, scoreboard numbers, and the club’s year drawn as one line from the outdoor season to indoor.

Leans on your wordsYear-round tennis. Energetic. Competitive when appropriate.

CWhites

Quiet, like tennis whites. White space, a single red net line, and 1951 set across it.

Leans on your wordsPlenty of white space. Modern. Professional.

The pages you have been clicking through wear Whites, with the serving courts borrowed from Clubhouse and the season line from Dome, so you have already seen a little of each in use. Tell us the letter. A mix is a fair answer too. Then we design the whole site in your choice and hand it over.

Try the three directions

Questions for the club

What we need to ask you

  1. Which direction?

    A Clubhouse, B Dome or C Whites. A mix is a fair answer too.

  2. Coaches

    Who is on the coaching team (names, titles, certifications, short bios), and when can we photograph them?

  3. This season

    What are the 2026/27 class days, times and fees for group lessons, and the league and camp dates?

  4. High Performance

    Is Transition Tour the group your site calls Future Elite? Which ages belong to each step?

  5. Photographs

    Can we book one photo session at the club, and do you have consent for the team photographs on your site?

  6. Non-members

    Do non-members pay for courts online, by phone or in person? Two of your pages differ.

  7. Policies

    Should the rules of conduct, media waiver and liability waiver have a page of their own?

  8. The Dome

    Do you call it the Dome or the Bubble?

  9. Brand and contacts

    Can you send the logo as vector files, and tell us which emails and phone numbers to publish, and who reads info@?

Thank you for a document that was a pleasure to build from.
